Important Questions.q:
Richard Hartshorne has recognized four distinct approaches to the study of political geography of a State, these are:-
 A. Power analysis approach 
 B. Historical approach 
 C. Geographical approach 
 D. Functional approach 
 E. Morphological approach 
 Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: A, B, C and D Only
A, B, C and E Only
A, B, D and E Only
B, C, D and E Only
Important Questions.explanation: (c) : Richard Hartshorne identified four distinct approaches for the study of the political geography of a state. These are – the power analysis approach, the historical approach, the functional approach, and the morphological approach. Hartshorne holds an important place in giving a systematic form to the study of political geography. He introduced a new approach in political geography which came to be known as the functional approach. Hartshorne conceived of a set of two major forces – centrifugal forces and centripetal forces, which constantly act upon the cohesion of a political unit. Hence, option (c) is correct.

Important Questions.explanation: The SI unit of Electric Resistance is Ohm (Ω). The SI unit of Electrical Resistivity (Specific Resistance) is Ohm-meter. Capacitance is measured in Farad (F). Magnetic Flux is measured in Weber (Wb). Electric Charge is measured in Coulomb (C). Additional Fact: Resistance vs. Resistivity: Resistance depends on the length and cross-sectional area of a conductor, whereas Resistivity is an intrinsic property of the material and its temperature (independent of shape or size). Magnetic Flux vs. Flux Density: While Magnetic Flux is Weber, Magnetic Flux Density is measured in Tesla (T) or Wb/m2. CGS Conversions (Frequently asked): The CGS unit for magnetic flux is the Maxwell. 1 Weber = 108 Maxwell. The CGS unit for magnetic flux density is Gauss. 1 Tesla = 104 Gauss. Coulomb / Ampere Link: Electric Current is the rate of flow of charge. Therefore, 1 Ampere = 1 Coulomb/second. One Coulomb contains approximately 6.24 x 1018 electrons. Farad Breakdown: 1 Farad = 1 Coulomb / 1 Volt. Because a Farad is a very large unit, practical capacitance is usually measured in microfarads (uF) or picofarads (pF).
